context.title: The King Who Ate Grass
context.summary: In his own words, Nebuchadnezzar tells of dreaming of a great tree cut down, ignoring Daniel's warning, losing his sanity and living like an animal, until he acknowledged the Most High and was restored.
context.background: The chapter is written as a royal proclamation. Babylonian building inscriptions show Nebuchadnezzar boasting of his great works in Babylon, and verse 30 captures exactly that pride. 'Seven times' (v. 25) is usually taken as seven years. In Aramaic Bibles verses 1–3 close chapter 3, so verse numbers differ from the KJV.

customs.note: Heavenly beings who carry out God's decrees, a term found only here in the Bible.

watchFor: The repeated lesson that 'the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men' (vv. 17, 25, 32).
Daniel's plea to 'break off thy sins by righteousness' (v. 27).
The king's praise at the end (vv. 34–37).

w: they will make known to me

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Daniel
people.summary: Beltis protect the king!, the Chaldee name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:7).

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

events.title: Prophecies of Daniel
events.summary: Passage: Daniel 1:1–12:13. People: Daniel. Lasted about 72 years.
